## Preface

This is the data collection script for the SDM NN. I originally used the environmental data in AusAMF and two other datasets, but I don't think I have enough environmental information to calculate distributions.

So, we are starting from scratch here.

The assumed working directory is the jobs folder.

## Libraries
```{r}
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(tidyterra)
```
## Projection Paths
```{r}
#Rorqual does not have internet access on the node I need, so I saved the tif grid for conversion to CRS 3577
local_grid = file.path("/home/herna499/links/projects/def-jstinchc/herna499/proj_data")

Sys.setenv(PROJ_DATA = local_grid)
Sys.setenv(PROJ_LIB  = local_grid)
Sys.setenv(PROJ_NETWORK = "OFF")
Sys.setenv(GDAL_HTTP_MAX_RETRY = "0")

message("PROJ Search Paths: ", paste(sf_proj_search_paths(), collapse = ", "))

sf_proj_network(enable = FALSE)
```


## AusAMF
AusAMF datasets that are likely to overlap with other data sources are prefaced with `AA_`

```{r}
# load in abundance matrices, metadata, and taxonomy
abundance = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/abundance_matrix.csv", row.names = 1)
AA_metadata = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/sample_metadata.csv")
AA_filtering = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/filtering_info.csv")
AA_taxonomy = read.csv("../raw_data/AusAMF/VT_taxonomy.csv")

# env_cube for environmental data from AusAMF
# input data for raster files is downloaded from the cited figshare in the manuscript
# https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28817378.v1
env_cube = rast("../raw_data/AusAMF/AusAMF_env_cube.tif")
env_cube = rename(env_cube, total_N = Total_N, avail_P = Avail_P, totalP = Total_P, elevation = Elevation, pH_cacl = pH) # this is just to keep names the same between the original metadata and that in the environmental cube. The mismatch is from the original paper.

# crop to match spatial extent of Australia
tocrop = terra::ext(112, 112+0.025*1681, -44, -44+0.025*1361)
env_cube = terra::crop(env_cube, tocrop)

# project data cube
AA_envcube = project(
  x = env_cube,
  y = "EPSG:3577",
  method = "bilinear",
  use_gdal = TRUE
)
```

## NVIS 7.0
This is the vegetation layer from NVIS V7.0. I will preface this data with `NV_`.
```{r}
# check available layers from `.gdb` file
gdb_path = "../raw_data/NVIS_V7/NVIS_V7_0_VECTOR_STATE_FILES_EXT.gdb/"
NV_avail_layers = st_layers(gdb_path)
NV_avail_layers$name

# create a list to store layers
# takes a looooooonnnngggg time
NV_layers = vect(gdb_path, proxy = TRUE)
NV_details = as.data.frame(vect(gdb_path, layer = NV_avail_layers$name[9]))
NV_flat = as.data.frame(vect(gdb_path, layer = NV_avail_layers$name[10]))
```
